newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican envoy finds "vibrant" Church in Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Vatican envoy finds "vibrant" Church in Kuwait.

text.p: The Vatican's foreign minister, during a visit to Kuwait, found a "vibrant and active" Roman Catholic Church made up almost entirely of foreigners working in the Moslem country, a spokesman said on Tuesday.

Monsignor Jean-Louis Tauran returned to the Vatican on Monday after a three-day visit to Kuwait where he met Church and government officials, chief Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls said in a statement.
Tauran reported that the Catholic community was "vibrant and active", although it had only seven priests, and enjoyed religious freedom, the statement said.

"In meetings with civil authorities, Monsignor Tauran stressed this positive fact many times. It is all the more important if seen in relation to other situations in the region, where Christians do not enjoy the same freedom," it added.
The statement did not elaborate. Saudi Arabia, which borders Kuwait, bans public Christian worship.

Navarro-Valls said the Roman Catholic community in Kuwait numbered about 100,000, predominantly foreign workers from India, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, Arab countries and western countries "with the execption of a few Kuwaiti families".
He said Tauran met Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah and Heir Apparent and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah as well as several government ministers.

"They discussed other subjects of a more general nature, which are constantly in the thoughts of Pope John Paul: the defence of life, peace, justice, solidarity and fundamental human rights," Navarro-Valls said.
